page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 976 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server provides 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a 54 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core and memory-intensive performance. The server achieves a PassMark CPU score of 54571.25 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16654.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 293.92 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations score 26047.32, also in the top 25%. Conversely, single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core score of 1852.19 and Geekbench single-core score of 1577.0, fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is measured at 150.66 GB/sec for read operations and 62.1 GB/sec for write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-64 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 15.25 GB per core, making it a specialized resource density option for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy single-threaded tasks. The lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which introduces an architectural tradeoff for I/O-heavy applications.

This hardware profile is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, heavy memory-cached web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks such as software compilation and image processing.
